LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The file is a standard Arch PKGBUILD for the `dinit` service manager, fetched from the project's own upstream release tarball on GitHub (`davmac314/dinit`, which matches the declared `url`). The `source` array uses a versioned release artifact (`v0.23.0`) with a pinned, concrete `sha256sums` entry — no `SKIP`, no VCS ref, no unreviewed download step.

`build()` runs the upstream `./configure` with ordinary flags (C++ standard, `--disable-strip`, platform, install prefixes) and then `make`. `check()` runs the project's own test targets, and `package()` does a plain `make DESTDIR="$pkgdir" install`. There is no `eval`, no encoded/obfuscated string, no `curl`/`wget` piping into a shell, no `git pull`/`fetch`+`reset`, no key/token/`shadow` access, and no network destination other than the project's own GitHub release URL. Nothing is written outside `$pkgdir` or `$srcdir`.

Minor hygiene notes only (not security findings): `arch` contains both `arm` and `aarch64` (`arm` is deprecated in Arch), and the `license` array lists `Apache` without a version, which is imprecise packaging metadata. Neither affects the safety of the build.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>Standard PKGBUILD, pinned checksum, upstream build only</summary>
</security_assessment>
